newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Labor Secretary asks UPS, Teamsters to meet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Labor Secretary asks UPS, Teamsters to meet.

text.p: Labour Secretary Alexis Herman said she called Teamsters President Ron Carey and United Parcel Service Chairman James Kelly Tuesday, urging they renew talks that broke off leading to the strike Monday.

"I spoke to both parties privately by telephone this afternoon and urged them both to go back to the bargaining table," she said in a statement. She said the talks were important for the company, its workers and their families, as well as other businesses.

"Federal mediation services continue to be available to both parties," Herman said. "These talks are important both for the one in 400 American workers who work directly for UPS, as well as the company itself, and for countless other businesses, workers and families who are directly and indrectly affected by negotiations."
President Clinton has so far ruled out federal intervention in the strike by 185,000 members of the Teamsters union at the nation's largest package delivery company.
Earlier in the day, Carey said he was ready to talk and that he wanted the secretary's help.
